requirements.label: required
requirements.title: Required courses
requirements.sourceText: Required courses: SOC 105 - Introduction to Sociology 3 credits; SOC 201 - Research Methods in Sociology 3 credits; SOC 202 - Statistical Methods in Sociology 3 credits; SOC 361 - Historical Development of Sociological Theory 3 credits

requirements.label: sociology-electives
requirements.title: Sociology electives
requirements.sourceText: In addition to the required courses above, students must complete an additional 18 credits of coursework (of which 15 credits must be upper division) from among all sociology course offerings. Note: Only six credits of independent study courses (SOC 447, SOC 487, SOC 488, SOC 495, SOC 496) may be used toward the requirements of 18 elective credits in sociology.

requirements.label: upper-division-electives
requirements.title: Upper-division credits within sociology electives

rule.text: Of the 18 sociology elective credits, 15 credits must be upper division.
rule.reason: Credit-level minimum within the elective pool cannot be expressed with the available constraints.

requirements.label: related-areas
requirements.title: Study in Related Areas

rule.text: At least three courses (nine credits, of which 6 credits must be upper division) chosen from one of the following related social sciences: Africana studies (only those courses with designator AFS), anthropology (only those courses with designator ANT), economics, history, linguistics, political science, psychology, and women's studies. Credits from applied social science professions such as social work, police science, education, and management science are not applicable.
rule.reason: Requires choosing one related area; subject designators for economics, history, linguistics and political science are not all stated on the page, and the upper-division minimum is a further credit rule.

requirements.label: upper-division-writing
requirements.title: Upper-Division Writing Requirement

rule.text: Fulfilled through SOC 361, which is also counted under the required courses and also satisfies the SBC WRTD requirement.
rule.reason: SOC 361 is already counted in the required courses and cannot be counted twice; this is a satisfied-by note rather than a separate credit rule.

requirements.sourceText: Sociology majors are expected to fulfill the upper-division writing requirement by the time of graduation. This requirement is met through SOC 361, the required Historical Development of Sociological Theory course, which also satisfies the SBC WRTD requirement.

policies.sourceText: All sociology courses completed for the major, except those graded S/U, must be passed with a letter grade of C or higher.
The Department of Sociology requires that transfer students take at least 12 credits in sociology in residence at Stony Brook to complete the sociology major.

notes.text: The upper-division writing requirement is met through SOC 361, which also satisfies the SBC WRTD requirement.
Transfer students must take at least 12 credits in sociology in residence at Stony Brook and may not transfer a sociology course with a grade lower than C for credit in the major.

Sociology Honors Program (not evaluated): open to seniors with a 3.50 GPA in the major and 3.20 overall who have completed or are completing the methods and statistics requirement and the upper-division writing requirement. Requires an approved proposal, SOC 495 in the first semester and SOC 496 in the second (six credits total). Honors are conferred if completed with distinction and the student has a 3.50 GPA in all sociology courses and 3.2 overall.

Students are encouraged to pursue minors of particular interest: Anthropology (ANT), Health, Medicine and Society (MHS), International Studies (INT), Political Science (POL), Women's and Gender Studies (WST).
